The passage supports every claim in the answer. It says rotational invariance comes from using interatomic distances dij = ∥ri − rj∥ as input to the filter network. It gives the radial basis expansion with the same formula, centers from 0 to 30 Å every 0.1 Å, and γ = 10 Å. It says the added non-linearity makes the initial filters less correlated and training faster. It also says the expanded distances go into two dense layers with softplus activations to compute W(ri − rj).

One claim is slightly loose. The answer says the distance "makes the filter rotationally invariant," while the passage says rotational invariance is "obtained by using interatomic distances … as input." This is effectively the same point. The answer also omits the reason for the expansion, which is that the filters would otherwise be highly correlated, but omitting that does not make anything it says unsupported.
